finding: Word operators now apply only to script suffixes, so real marker matches in .yaml, .yml and .html pass the check.
why: Acceptance says the check fails on code that matches a marker by substring, but this change silences the prose false positive `marker: X in file` by dropping all word-operator detection for those suffixes; D-13 discloses this but quotes no Acceptance or SDD passage in Supersedes, and no such file exists in the tree yet.
fix: Keep word operators for every CODE_SUFFIXES file and exempt only the prose shape, for example a YAML scalar or HTML text outside `run:`, `if:` and `<script>`.
evidence: Probe of HEAD~1 against HEAD: `a.yaml run: grep "afkv2-core-behaviors" out.txt` old=True new=False; `a.yml if: "'afkv2-core-behaviors' in github.event.head_commit.message"` old=True new=False; `a.html <script>if ("afkv2-core-behaviors" in text) go()</script>` old=True new=False. Code: `return suffix in SCRIPT_SUFFIXES and SUBSTRING_WORD.search(line) is not None`.

finding: The slice pattern now rejects any bracket that holds a quote, so a prefix compare that slices with `len("...")` passes the check.
why: To stop flagging the key lookup `d["a:b"] == x`, the change dropped a case the prior commit caught; D-13's premise "a slice with a quote inside the brackets is a key lookup, not a slice" is false for this input, which breaks the Acceptance bullet on prefix matches.
fix: Exempt only a bracket whose whole content is one quoted string: `\[(?!\s*["'][^"']*["']\s*\])[^\]]*:[^\]]*\]\s*[!=]=`, apply the same change at line 46, and add this input to the failing cases.
evidence: Probe: `line[:len("afkv2-core-behaviors")] == "afkv2-core-behaviors"` old=True new=False. The proposed pattern gave True for `line[:len("m")] == "m"` and `line[:20] == "m"`, and False for `d["a:b"] == x`, `d["a:b"] == "m"` and `d['a:b'] != x`.

finding: The URL scrub removes every non-space character after a URL, so a v1 name on the same token passes the no-v1-name rule.
why: `URL = https?://\S+` runs to the next whitespace, so `fetch("https://x/"+AFK_KEY)` or minified JSON `{"url":"https://x.y","env":"AFK_KEY"}` reports no v1 name (AC-019), and D-13 does not list this gap.
fix: Stop the URL match at a quote, bracket, comma or semicolon, for example `https?://[^\s"'`,;()<>]+`, and add both lines to the failing test cases.
evidence: Inline probe of `_holds_v1_name(URL.sub('', line), is_code)`: 'fetch("https://x/"+AFK_KEY)' True -> False; '{"url":"https://x.y","env":"AFK_KEY"}' False -> False; 'url="https://x.y";afk_key=1' True -> False.

finding: The Python spellings of the marker rule miss slices with a call or index in the chain, and regex methods on a compiled pattern.
why: The slice alternatives accept only `name[a:b] ==` and `== name[a:b]`, and `findall`/`sub` need a literal `re.` before them, so these prefix or substring matches pass (SDD §7 defect row); D-13 says the list is finite, but these forms are of the kinds the delta claims to catch.
fix: Let the reversed slice accept a call or index chain, flag a slice followed by a method before the compare, and move `findall|finditer|sub|subn` into the `\.(?:...)\(` method list.
evidence: Inline probe of `MARKER_TOKEN.search(line) and _is_partial_match(line, '.py')`, each False: '"afkv2-core-behaviors" == line.strip()[:20]'; '"afkv2-core-behaviors" == lines[0][:20]'; 'line[:20].strip() == "afkv2-core-behaviors"'; 're.compile(r"afkv2-core-behaviors").findall(text)'; 're.compile(r"afkv2-core-behaviors").sub("",text)'. Control: 'line.strip()[:20] == "afkv2-core-behaviors"' True.

finding: The marker rule misses the usual cmd, bash and PowerShell substring forms, in the languages the plugin's hooks and scripts can use.
why: `%\w+:~` and `-[ci]?(?:not)?(?:like|match|contains)` cover only one form per shell, so the batch substring test `if not "%line:afkv2-core-behaviors=%"=="%line%"`, delayed `!line:~0,20!`, bash `=~`, `${line:0:20}`, `${line#...}` and PowerShell `-replace`/`-split` all pass the check.
fix: Add `[%!]\w+:` for cmd, `=~` and `\$\{\w+(?::|#|%)` for bash, and `-[ci]?(?:replace|split)\b` for PowerShell, each with a failing test row.
evidence: Inline probe, each False: 'if not "%line:afkv2-core-behaviors=%"=="%line%" echo y' (.cmd); 'if "!line:~0,20!"=="afkv2-core-behaviors" echo y' (.cmd); '[[ "$line" =~ afkv2-core-behaviors ]]' (.sh); '[ "${line:0:20}" = "afkv2-core-behaviors" ]' (.sh); 'x="${line#afkv2-core-behaviors}"' (.sh); '$line -replace "afkv2-core-behaviors",""' (.ps1); '$line -split "afkv2-core-behaviors"' (.ps1).

finding: D-13 puts a second fork, the narrowing of the marker rule, inside the Chosen line of a v1-name decision, with no options and no Supersedes quote.
why: The protocol fixes `Chosen: {option} — {one-sentence evidence}` and says a Supersedes line overrides only the exact passage it quotes, so the narrowing of D-4 and of SDD §7 is not on the record as a supersession.
fix: Append a separate D-n for the marker-rule narrowing, with its own options, and quote the D-4 operator sentence and the SDD §7 row "no substring or prefix marker match in afkv2 code" in Supersedes.
evidence: Root DECISIONS.md: "A `Supersedes:` line overrides the exact spec passage it quotes". D-13 title: "the no-v1-name rule becomes one pattern plus one prose exception". D-13 Chosen holds: "Same-line marker rule: ... word operators ... apply only to script files, and a slice with a quote inside the brackets is a key lookup". D-13 Supersedes names only D-6 and D-10.

finding: Possible gap: every suffix outside the code list takes the prose exception, not only `.md`, `.txt` and `.json` as D-13 states, so a bare v1 word passes in any unlisted script or config file.
why: The SDD rule is "`afk` or `AFK_` not followed by `v2`", and D-13 names only `.md`, `.txt` and `.json` as the prose-word gap, but unlisted suffixes pass too and also skip the marker check; `test_code_suffixes_are_the_recorded_set` pins the list.
fix: Invert the choice: add a `PROSE_SUFFIXES` set of `.md`, `.txt` and `.json`, apply the prose exception only to those, and use `CODE_SUFFIXES` only for the rule that an undecodable file is a problem.
evidence: Probe of `_holds_v1_name` with the suffix test: `a.psm1 afk = 1`, `a.pyw afk = 1`, `a.ini afk = 1` and `a.cfg afk: 1` all gave new=False. The marker probe `a.psm1 $line -match "afkv2-core-behaviors"` gave new=False. Line 86: `is_code = path.suffix.lower() in CODE_SUFFIXES`. D-13: "a prose-shaped word in `.md`, `.txt` and `.json`".

finding: The no-data-folder test goes blind once the root folder exists, and one failing run creates that folder.
why: If the guard `if not defined LOCALAPPDATA exit /b 0` is lost, the first run makes `\afkv2` on the drive root with no cleanup, so the second parametrized hook and every later run compare True == True and pass while the hook still writes its record there.
fix: Snapshot the folder contents and record modification times before the run and compare them after, or skip with a clear reason when the folder exists before the run.
evidence: `existed_before = root_folder.exists()` ... `assert root_folder.exists() == existed_before`; the previous version refused the run with `assert not root_folder.exists(), f"{root_folder} exists before the run; remove it"`. By reading: no write to C:\afkv2 was run; `ls C:/afkv2` reports no such folder now.

finding: Many operators in the rewritten marker rule have no failing case, including `.match(` and all of the `re.` alternative.
why: Acceptance requires failure on a prefix or substring marker match, but `.match(` (the usual Python prefix match), `.split(`, `.replace(`, `.count(`, `.contains(` and the new `matchall`, `replaceall` and `subn` can leave the regex with every test still passing.
fix: Add one failing case per operator in the regex, including `re.match`, `re.findall` and `re.sub`, or build the parametrization from a literal list of every operator.
evidence: In-memory probe over the 38 failing and 7 passing cases from the parametrize marks: method ops uncovered ['rfind','index','rindex','count','match','matchall','split','partition','replace','replaceall','lastindexof','contains']; re ops uncovered ['findall','finditer','sub','subn']; `drop alt 1 \bre\.(?:findall|finditer|sub| SURVIVES`; word op 'strstr' has no case.

finding: The script/data split in `SCRIPT_SUFFIXES` is not pinned; only the union is, so `.sh` can lose the `grep`, `sed` and `awk` rule with all tests passing.
why: D-13 applies word operators only to script files, but those operators are tested only on `.py`, `.cmd` and `.ps1`, and `grep`, `sed` and `awk` run only in `sample.py` because line 309 forces that name, so moving `.sh`, `.bat`, `.js` or `.ts` to the data group goes unnoticed.
fix: Assert `SCRIPT_SUFFIXES` as a literal set, and move the shell lines to the (name, line) form with `sample.sh` and `sample.bat`, which also removes the `if` at line 309.
evidence: Probe: `SCRIPT_SUFFIXES minus` .bat, .cjs, .js, .jsx, .mjs, .sh, .ts, .tsx, .vue each SURVIVES; word ops -> suffixes {'in':['.py'],'findstr':['.cmd'],'find':['.py'],'grep':['.py'],'sed':['.py'],'awk':['.py'],'sls':['.ps1']}. Test line: `assert plugin_check.CODE_SUFFIXES == {...}`.

finding: The new reverse-order slice alternative has no key-lookup negative, so its quote exclusion is unproven.
why: D-13 says `a slice with a quote inside the brackets is a key lookup, not a slice`, but the passing cases cover only the `d["a:b"] == x` order, so removing the exclusion from `[!=]==?\s*[\w.$]+\[...\]` passes every case and would flag `"marker" == d["a:b"]`; the lookbehind `(?<![=!<>])` on word operators is also unpinned.
fix: Add a passing case `f'"{MARKER}" == d["a:b"]'` and a passing case that exercises the word-operator lookbehind, or remove that lookbehind if no input needs it.
evidence: Probe: `alt4 allow quote in key (reverse form) SURVIVES`; `word lookbehind dropped SURVIVES`; `alt3 allow quote in key (first form) killed`; on the real code `'"afkv2-core-behaviors" == d["a:b"]'` is not flagged.

finding: The new NUL branch in `_read_lines` is tested only for code files; no case covers a text file outside code that decodes with NUL characters.
why: `test_binary_file_outside_code_is_skipped` uses `b"\xff\xfe\x00"`, which fails decoding at byte 0 and never reaches `if "\x00" in text`, so changing line 218 to always report a problem passes, and the silent skip of a UTF-16-LE `.md` holding a v1 name is not pinned as a decision.
fix: Add a case with a UTF-16-LE `.md` and a NUL-holding UTF-8 `.png`, asserting the chosen result, and record the skip as a known gap if it stays.
evidence: Probe: `b"\xff\xfe\x00".decode("utf-8")` raises at position 0; `_read_lines(a.md utf-16-le with the v1 env prefix, False)` returns `([], None)` and `check_no_v1_names` reports nothing for that file. The mutant was not run; the claim that it survives comes from reading the parametrize lists.

finding: The PowerShell operator alternative also matches inside a marker token, so a legal afkv2 name fails the check.
why: `-[ci]?(?:not)?(?:like|match|contains)\b` has no lookbehind and the same text is the marker token, so `.afkv2-match { color: red }` or `class="afkv2-card-like"` reports a prefix or substring match with no matching code on the line.
fix: Add a lookbehind `(?<![\w-])` so the operator needs a space or other non-name character before its dash.
evidence:
Inline probe: a.css '.afkv2-match { color: red }' True; a.html '
' True. Regex line: `r"|-[ci]?(?:not)?(?:like|match|contains)\b"`.

finding: A text file outside the code suffixes that is not UTF-8 skips the no-v1-name rule with no problem reported.
why: `_read_lines` returns no lines and no reason for a non-code file, so a UTF-16 `.json` or `.md`, or a Latin-1 extensionless script, that holds `AFK_KEY` passes AC-019, and D-13 does not list this gap (not run; read from the code).
fix: For an undecodable non-code file, search the raw bytes and the NUL-stripped bytes for the v1 name, so true binaries still pass.
evidence: `except UnicodeDecodeError:\n    return [], "not UTF-8; the check cannot read it" if is_code else None` and the same return for `"\x00" in text`; `is_code` comes from `path.suffix.lower() in CODE_SUFFIXES`, which holds no `.json`, `.md`, `.txt` or empty suffix.

finding: Possible duplicated code: `_read_lines` holds the same return twice, and its message says "not UTF-8" for a NUL in text that decoded as valid UTF-8.
why: The two copies can drift, and a valid UTF-8 file that holds a NUL gets a wrong reason.
fix: Use one path for both cases, and word the reason so it also covers a NUL, for example "not UTF-8 text".
evidence: Lines 216 and 218 are the same: `return [], "not UTF-8; the check cannot read it" if is_code else None`. Line 217: `if "\x00" in text:`.

finding: The boundaries of the D-13 prose exception are only partly tested.
why: D-13 lists a quote before the word and `)`, `;`, `!`, `?`, or `.` or `:` at line end after it, but no case uses them, so narrowing the exception passes the tests and would fail ordinary documentation such as a sentence ending in the word.
fix: Add passing prose cases for each listed neighbour character, including the word followed by `.` at line end and by `)`, and a strict xfail for the recorded `notafk` gap in the style of line 424.
evidence: Probe mutants of `V1_PROSE_WORD`: `drop dot/colon EOL SURVIVES`, `drop ; ! ? SURVIVES`, `drop single quote before SURVIVES`, `drop ) after SURVIVES`; `V1_NAME lookbehind dropped SURVIVES`.

finding: No test uses an upper-case suffix, so `.lower()` in both checks is unpinned.
why: `path.suffix.lower()` in `check_no_v1_names` and `check_marker_matching` handles names such as `X.CMD` on Windows, but every sample name is lower case, so removing `.lower()` passes every case and the file drops to the prose rule or is skipped by the marker rule.
fix: Add one `sample.CMD` case to the bare-word test and one to the marker-match test.
evidence: Enumeration with `grep -n 'sample\.[A-Z]'` over test_plugin_check.py: no hit; all names are `sample{suffix}` from the lower-case set or literal lower-case names. Probe: real code flags `c.CMD:1: v1 name: set ...`. The mutant was not run; the claim that it survives comes from reading the test lists.
